steps.content: At the sound of your voice, she slowly moves toward you. The silver bell at her waist sings with each step, soft and clear, and with every chime, the darkness that has pressed so long upon your heart finally loosens its grip.
Dazed, you watch her crouch before you. She takes your hand.

steps.speaker: Woman's Voice
steps.content: You're awake. No need for fear. I'm here.

The sharp sound of tearing bandages gives way to the gentle pressure of a fresh dressing. Then, through the thin fabric, you feel another's warmth, solid and real. Only now can you be certain: you have finally left that place where only ghosts wander.
A deep relaxation settles into your bones. Reaching out, you loosely grasp her sleeve and catch the faint, bittersweet scent of medicine clinging to her.
Wait... Those clothes?!
[Transition for 1s, screen violently shakes]

You spring up, but your body isn't listening. You stagger back, steps wild and uncoordinated. When your foot hooks on something, there's no stopping the fall. You hit the ground hard, tailbone first, the sharp pain a sudden, brutal clarity.

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: Such alarm, young friend. Whatever for?
The voice calls out once more, and a cold sweat slicks your body in an instant. Before thought can become action, you hear the approach—the wet, squelching tread of her shoes against the mud.
Pain lances through your head as you force your blurred eyes to focus, to lock onto her. There is no error. That is an Eastian robe, identical to the one that woman wore.

The memory of bells chimes in your ears, bringing with it the return of the sinister whispers and that putrid stench. Against your limbs, something begins to creep, writhing and tightening, a phantom grip trying to drag you back to that place.
You thrash wildly at the empty air, legs scrabbling against the ground as you fight to push yourself backward. But for all your desperate efforts, you've barely managed to move half a meter.
Then she stops before you. Her shadow falls, swallowing you whole. There is nowhere left to run.
Don't... don't come any...
The sound that tears from your throat barely resembles your own voice anymore.

She lowers her gaze, studying you for a long, thoughtful moment. Then something shifts in her eyes. She raises her fingers in a delicate pinching gesture and begins to speak, her words slow and deliberate.

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: Yin energy clings to you. Your spirit's gone to pieces. I fear some evil work. Not good. Not good at all.
As she speaks, her hand reaches out and closes firmly around your shoulder.
The hand doesn't budge. Instead, she uses your own momentum against you, flipping you over completely. An arm hooks under your armpit, scooping you up and tucking you against her side like a parcel.
Her arm digs painfully into your chest. Your legs kick helplessly in the air, but the struggle only makes her grip tighten further.

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: Keep squirming, young friend, and I'll have to make you less comfortable.
She raises the other hand and waves it in front of your face. From nothing, golden threads kindle across her palm, glowing, gathering.
No, you won't let her have you. Not completely.
You coil inward—arms folding, body curling—and writhe against her grip, desperate to slip loose.
Nngh...

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: Still stubborn. Very well, don't blame me for what comes.
Her hand cuts through the air, forming a seal. Then, pressure. Invisible, omnidirectional, crushing in on you from everywhere at once.
She adjusts you against her side like someone shifting a bag, and the casualness of it makes your stomach turn. You are nothing to her but weight. Her voice rises:

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: According to The Scripture of Purifying the Heart, to dispel nightmares, one must press the philtrum with the left hand twenty-seven times...
Twenty-seven?!

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: ...And recite the heart-purifying incantation and beseech the Divine's protection...

Suddenly, she stops. With a slow shake of her head, her expression shifts to one of grave alarm. Her hand gropes behind her back, finally producing a rolled booklet. With a sharp flick of her wrist, it unfurls with an audible swoosh, and she starts flipping pages in a desperate hurry.
...Don't tell me you forgot the incantation.
Smack. The booklet is slapped hard against your lips. The musty odor of decaying paper invades your senses, thick and suffocating.

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: Nonsense. The phantoms in your dreams must've scrambled your wits, young friend. Hence this babble.

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: This incantation, that incantation... what does it matter? Sincerity is what counts. As long as it saves you.
With that, she simply stuffs the booklet back behind her, clears her throat, and reaches toward the area beneath your nose.

Her murmuring drifts into your ears—first, fragments about "Lord of the Great White," then an invocation: "spirits of heaven, spirits of earth." And then... all those murmurs give way to a humming tune.
All the while, her thumb works against your philtrum in erratic, pounding jabs. Barely ten presses, but each one feels strong enough to drive your teeth through your gums.

You gather yourself to protest, but her voice cuts off. In the same breath, a small bottle appears in her hand, and its contents splash across your face. Ash-tainted water hits you, and your whole body shudders.
Cough... cough cough... Are you done yet?! Sto—

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: Wisdom pure and clear, spirit at peace... Begone!
[White Flash]

Warmth blooms from your philtrum, gentle at first, then rippling through your limbs like thaw after deep cold. Your mind sharpens, suddenly clear. The whispers, the phantom touches, the creeping dread—all of it withdraws like a retreating tide.
You blink. Desolate ruins resolve before you. Wind moans through broken stone, hollow and gloomy, but now the sound brings only stillness. Only peace.

When did she set you down? You're seated now, cross-legged on the ground. The talisman water still drips from your chin, cold against your skin. And there she is, watching you with that pleased, squinty-eyed smile.

steps.speaker: Daoist
steps.content: There we go. That's twice now I've lent you a hand. Surely you can drop your guard and hear me out?
She rests her chin on one hand and extends the other toward you, but gently now, without command. Her palm simply waits, open and patient.

You're still foggy, but your hand lifts on its own, finding hers. Her palm is cool against your skin, soft. And beneath it, a pulse ticks gently against your fingers. Not a ghost. Not a corpse. Alive.
She draws you up, steady and sure, until you're standing.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I'm <color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>. Young friend, do you remember me?
